Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I'm copying Stephanie from Security and Vivek from Ops for any technical clarifications. I can put these into a one-page write-up for the SIG.

- Notification window: Redwood's operating target is to acknowledge incidents within 2 hours of a confirmed detection and to provide an initial customer notification within 72 hours when the incident constitutes unauthorized access/exfiltration of customer data.
- POC: primary inbox security@redwood.com; for escalations the on-call phone (used for severity >=2) is managed by the IR rotation — I'll confirm the phone contact in the follow-up.
- Evidence: we can provide timeline exports, access/audit logs, and redacted request traces. Full packet captures are provided in limited circumstances and require a legal request + protective order; retention depends on log policies (we include retention in the attached SOC2_Summary).
- Sign-off: legal + Head of Security must approve formal regulator-facing notices; we can commit to an internal coordination timeline for expedited requests.

I'm attaching a short IR process PDF that you can include with the SIG. Proposed next step: 30-min sync Thursday to confirm any account-specific retention caveats.

Tessa — answers below, feel free to copy/paste into the SIG.

1) SLAs we publish internally: acknowledge within 2 hours of confirmed detection; initial customer notification within 72 hours for incidents involving customer data; follow-up updates at 24/72/weekly cadence depending on severity. We indicate in SIG that time-to-remediation varies by case.

2) On-call policy: 24/7 IR rotation, primary on-call acknowledges within 2 hours and coordinates triage. For external-facing phone escalation (severity >=2) we provide an on-call escalation number; for SIG we provide the security@redwood.com email and the on-call escalation phone as "available on request" (we don't publish direct phone numbers in the questionnaire).

3) Evidence artifacts: timeline CSV (event IDs + timestamps), access/audit logs (redacted to PII scope), request traces (redacted), configuration snapshots, and IAM role change logs. Packet captures or raw DB dumps are provided only with a legal process and with a secure transfer agreement. Evidence is staged to a locked S3 bucket with time-limited presigned URLs and MFA-protected access for customers.

4) Legal/POA: anything that could include third-party PII or carrier data requires redaction or a signed data-sharing agreement. For regulator-facing materials we escalate to Legal + Head of Security for sign-off.

Addendum: retention windows vary by log type; include SOC2_Summary.xlsx for the retention matrix (attached).

—Vivek Kulkarni
